task: Record why local git and the GitHub API disagree on whether causal-graph.json merges cleanly, and what the safe resolution is. Ordering in workLog is sequential; the timestamps mark order only, not measured wall-clock times.

events.content: Observed PR #3636 reporting CONFLICTING while git merge-tree exited 0 against the same two commits.
Polled gh pr view four times at 30 second intervals on the correct head SHA.
Ran a throwaway worktree merge of origin/main.
Checked git check-attr and git config for a custom merge driver on the graph.
Merged origin/main into the branch and pushed, then compared node counts across HEAD, HEAD^1, and HEAD^2.
Tested whether the finding generalizes by diagnosing PR #3497, which had also gone CONFLICTING.
Searched .serena/memories/git/ and the driver docstring for existing coverage of the GitHub side symptom.
Commit: 6e906b4e42
Observed PR #3636 reporting mergeable CONFLICTING/DIRTY while a local merge of the same commits was clean. Polled gh pr view four times at 30 second intervals on the reported head SHA.
Ran an adversarial review of that draft on a different model family (gpt-5.6-sol) with a prompt that specifically attacked the causal claim and asked which confounds were not ruled out.
Checked GitHub's reported base against the head for PR #3636: git merge-base --is-ancestor 87b1176674 cadd47a5b1.

Ran a controlled experiment against the advanced main (304355e98f), which is not an ancestor: merge-tree with the driver active, with the driver forced to false, with the driver replaced by a plain text merge, and a raw git merge-file of the three blobs.
Verified the review's remaining technical claims against the source rather than accepting them.
Replaced the whole-record comparison with an identity-key comparison using the driver's own _COLLECTIONS keys, then re-checked PR #3636's merge.

Rewrote the memory around the finding the existing runbook does not cover: for a driver-managed path, a local trial merge is not authoritative for GitHub in either direction, because GitHub runs no custom merge driver.

Rebased the branch onto main after PR #3643 removed the Tier 3 causal memory graph, then reworked the deliverable. PR #3643 deleted .agents/memory/causality/causal-graph.json, scripts/validation/merge_causal_graph.py, .claude/skills/memory/scripts/update_causal_graph.py, scripts/maintenance/install_merge_drivers.py, and the causal-graph entry in .gitattributes, so every worked example in the draft named a file that no longer exists on main.

Walked the claim instead of asserting it. Built a scratch repository carrying this repository's .gitattributes and merged divergent edits to .agents/HANDOFF.md and .agents/handoffs/b.md against a plain text-attributed control, then ran a second scratch repository contrasting merge=union against merge=ours on git 2.43.0.

Ran an adversarial review of the rewritten memory and runbook bullet on a different model family (gpt-5.6-sol) with instructions to falsify each claim independently and reproduce every experiment in its own scratch repositories.

The memory-size pre-commit hook rejected the single memory at 11211 characters against a 10000 maximum, and reported six categories against a maximum of five. Split the file on the seam between the two findings it carried rather than trimming evidence.

Ran a second adversarial review of the split memories on gpt-5.6-sol, then reproduced each finding locally with a merge driver that succeeds and writes a sentinel, because a failing driver cannot discriminate between running and absent.
Published the rebased branch without a force push, then found a second staleness mode on the PR itself.
